name: _cast_Long
description: Representative ATen schema, copied verbatim: "aten::_cast_Long(Tensor self, bool non_blocking=False) -> Tensor". This representative signature is NOT exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and this definition must never be used to narrow, drop or adapt that coverage. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: ["aten::_cast_Long(Tensor self, bool non_blocking=False) -> Tensor"]. Semantics derived from the tests: elementwise cast of a tensor to torch.int64; floating-point inputs truncate toward zero, and int/bool inputs are converted to int64. The one-argument call form covers the schema default non_blocking=False, and both positional and keyword spellings with False and True are exercised. For an int64 input the native cast is a zero-copy alias that returns the input tensor object itself (the test asserts res_out is inp), while for every other dtype the input is read out of place, so the source values must survive; this aliasing is conditional on the input dtype, and the selected schema records no alias and no mutation, so no alias or mutation effect is expressed here. View layouts (slice, transpose, offset, expand), empty and zero-extent tensors, dtype eligibility, FP8/FP64 exact and boundary values, and the implementation-defined mapping of non-finite/out-of-int64-range floats (compared against the native device result) are all defined by the original pytest. Error behavior (non-bool non_blocking, extra positional argument, out= keyword, missing operand, non-tensor self) remains enforced by the original pytest.
